newsitem.title: POLAND: BPH HOPES TO FIND INVESTOR BY Q1 1997.
newsitem.headline: BPH HOPES TO FIND INVESTOR BY Q1 1997.

text.p: Poland's Bank Przemyslowo- Handlowy (BPH) hopes to find a buyer for the treasury's current 46.6 percent stake in the first quarter of 1997, the Gazeta Wyborcza daily quoted the bank's president as saying.
Henryka Pieronkiewicz said the bank wanted to find a strategic investor, who would also rise the bank's share capital, as quickly as possible.
"The speed is important, because the bank wants to draw capital from international financial markets, which currently views Polish securities very warmly," Pieronkiewicz said.
She also said the bank was condsidering a convertible bond issue, which could be bought by an investor, who would prefer not to immediatley committ himself to a stake in the bank.
Wyborcza quoted Pieronkiewicz as saying the bank was also considering a merger with another big bank earmarked for privatisation, such as Bank Zachodni SA and Powszechny Bank Kredytowy.
The group could later take over smaller banks, she said.
BPH is one of Poland's top 10 banks in terms of capital and assets.

The bank, privatised in January 1995, has said it would like to be privatised by selling a stake to a strategic investor after the government dropped it from its banking consolidation programme in May.
Earlier Pieronkiewicz has said the treasury was likely to sell about 41 percent of the bank's shares.

Among BPH's other major shareholders are the Euroepan Bank for Reconstruction and Development with a 15.06 percent stake, and ING Barings and its subsidiary Bank Slaski with a joint 12.6 percent stake.
